standard.title: Plan and deliver analytical presentations
standard.description: plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations for purpose and audience, using language features, literary devices and features of voice such as volume, tone, pitch and pace, and organising, expanding and developing ideas in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive, analytical and/or critical
standard.prior_knowledge: Students plan, create and deliver presentations selecting structures, devices and voice features for purpose and audience (AC9E7LY07). They have not yet developed analytical and critical spoken modes, or deliberately coordinated literary devices, language features and voice features simultaneously.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations using language features, literary devices and voice features for purposes and audiences across analytical and critical modes.

nodes.label: Planning for spoken analytical and critical purposes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a spoken presentation with a clear structure that develops and expands ideas analytically or critically for a specific audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a spoken presentation with a clear purpose, a structure that develops ideas, and deliberate selection of at least one text structure suited to the purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Plan a spoken presentation that organises, expands and develops ideas — selecting text structures and adapting literary devices to meet the needs of the audience when debating, presenting a seminar or creating a voiceover.
wider: Compare planning strategies for a formal seminar versus a debate — identifying what structural choices differ and why the audience and form demand different organisation
Plan a collaborative imaginative recreation of a text or key idea, identifying how collaboration requires explicit structural negotiation

response_modes.reason: Planning analytical spoken texts requires students to reason about how ideas should be organised for an audience that cannot re-read. The reasoning scaffold — what the audience needs to hear first, how to signal transitions, how to use voice to mark structure — differs from written planning and needs explicit modelling.

success_criteria: Student produces a plan with a clear purpose and structure suited to the spoken form
Student can explain at least one planning decision in terms of what the audience needs
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot plan a spoken text for audience cannot meaningfully rehearse voice features at N2 — without a planned structure there is nothing to rehearse against, and delivery at N3 is unfocused.

nodes.label: Rehearsing voice features for effect
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can rehearse a presentation using voice features — volume, tone, pitch and pace — for specific effects and can articulate the relationship between voice choice and purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Rehearse a section of a presentation varying at least one voice feature (volume, tone, pitch or pace) for effect, and explain what effect the variation is intended to create.
nodes.typical_width: Select voice features — tone, volume, pitch and pace — for their specific effects to create tone or persuade an audience, demonstrating deliberate rehearsal decisions.
wider: Compare how the same words land differently with different voice feature choices — conducting a side-by-side rehearsal and evaluating the effect
Analyse how professional speakers (e.g. in the elaboration examples: news voiceovers, debates) use voice features, and evaluate which choices could be transferred to a student presentation

response_modes.reason: Voice feature control develops through rehearsal practice. Students know conceptually that pace and tone create effects but the skill of deploying them consistently under performance conditions requires rehearsal repetition, not additional conceptual knowledge.

success_criteria: Student demonstrates deliberate variation of at least one voice feature in delivery
Student can explain the intended effect of at least one voice feature choice

nodes.label: Delivering with integrated multimodal and language choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can deliver a spoken or multimodal presentation that integrates language features, literary devices, voice features and multimodal elements for purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Deliver a presentation that integrates at least two of the four elements (language features, literary devices, voice features, multimodal elements) in ways that serve the purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Deliver a spoken or multimodal presentation integrating language features, literary devices, voice features and multimodal elements — including graphics, text animations or images to accompany and influence viewer response.
wider: Deliver a news-style current affairs presentation that uses images with spoken text to influence viewer response, then evaluate how effectively the multimodal combination achieved the purpose
Collaborate with peers to deliver an imaginative recreation of part of a text — evaluating how the group's delivery decisions collectively represent the key idea

response_modes.reason: Delivery integrates all four elements simultaneously under performance conditions. Coordinating language choices, device deployment, voice features and multimodal elements while maintaining audience connection is the fullest expression of the descriptor's demand.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multimodal presentation delivery is directly connected to digital media literacy and real-world communication. The elaborations include news-format production and collaborative performance — both are rich and motivating contexts for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student delivers a presentation that demonstrates deliberate integration of at least two of the four element types
Student can evaluate the success of at least one integrative choice — did it serve the purpose and audience?
